data.content: The British government supported the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Kosovo for a campaign against violence, and the Ministry of Justice asked us to contribute to the creation of an awareness campaign.
Understanding the importance of such an initiative, we worked diligently to ensure that the message was communicated effectively and had an impact.

We worked on changing the narrative from “It’s not my problem” to “It’s my problem.” The goal was to emphasize that when we witness violence, we should not ignore it or think it is someone else’s issue, but we must take action. It is our collective responsibility to intervene and bring about change.

An orange line runs through the word “NOT” to visualize the rejection of passivity. Orange was chosen to symbolize urgency and action, but also internationally recognized as the color against violence.

We created five television spots (TVCs) with different themes:
Reporting abuse when a neighbor is part of the violence;
When our friends harass or disrespect girls and women;
Abuse online;
When a girl is harassed on the street;
Domestic violence.
We also prepared texts for radio, worked on social networks, and billboards.
Each platform had a unique approach
To ensure the campaign reaches and resonates with the diverse population of Kosovo, all materials were translated and adapted into four languages: Albanian, Serbian, Romani, and English.
